domain: Theological Ethics / Technology Governance / Philosophical Anthropology
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested commitment to 'safeguarding the human person in the age of AI' as articulated across Catholic magisterial teaching, secular liberal governance frameworks, and transhumanist/posthumanist movements. The shared kernel—human dignity must be protected as AI advances—is read through incompatible foundational axioms about what constitutes the human person, producing structurally different constraints on AI development, enhancement technologies, and the boundaries of permissible transformation.

key_entities: Catholic Magisterium (authoritative teaching body grounding dignity in imago Dei)
Secular liberal governance bodies (rights-based regulatory frameworks)
AI systems (technological substrate under normative contestation)
key_tensions: Imago Dei (fixed divine image) vs posthumanist continuity (enhancement as fulfillment)
Technocratic paradigm critique vs enhancement optimism

Lens diversity probe suggests yes, but extraction from provided context insufficient to characterize.
omegas.source: §1.3-K lens diversity requirement + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Does the dignity kernel extend to non-human animals or sentient AI? All three readings assume human exceptionalism but differ on enhancement; a fourth reading (sentientist) would challenge the boundary itself.

How do dignity constraints bind when authority structures conflict? If EU regulation (autonomy-rights) bans enhancement that Vatican (imago Dei) also opposes but transhumanist jurisdictions permit, which constraint governs?
At what capability level does AI transition from tool (all readings permit) to person-competitor (readings diverge)? The threshold itself is contested and may be a fourth axis.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Human dignity must be safeguarded as artificial intelligence advances
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Magisterial teaching (Catholic), democratic regulatory bodies (secular liberal), scientific/market consensus (transhumanist)

readings.commitment: Dignity is the inviolable image of the Triune God, equal in all persons prior to any capability
readings.authority_grounding: Magisterial teaching, natural law, theological anthropology
readings.expected_structural_delta: AI must remain tool subordinate to human person; enhancement and superintelligence categorically rejected as violations of created order; victim set includes any human subjected to technocratic reduction or transhumanist transformation

readings.commitment: Dignity is grounded in human autonomy, rationality, and rights rather than divine image
readings.authority_grounding: Liberal democratic theory, secular bioethics, human rights frameworks
readings.expected_structural_delta: AI governance through transparency, accountability, labor/privacy protection; cautious openness to enhancement within rights limits; victim set includes those whose autonomy or rights are violated by opaque or coercive AI systems

readings.commitment: The human is not a fixed limit; cognitive/biological enhancement and superintelligence are continuous with flourishing
readings.authority_grounding: Transhumanist philosophy, longtermist ethics, scientific progressivism
readings.expected_structural_delta: Enhancement and 'more than human' futures are fulfillment not threat; dignity attaches to persons however constituted; victim set includes those denied access to enhancement or constrained by biological limits

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single coherent framework can hold both 'human nature is a fixed divine image that must not be transgressed' and 'human nature is a contingent biological substrate open to enhancement and transcendence.' Accepting the imago Dei axiom as true requires rejecting posthumanist continuity as false.

Partial contradiction: imago Dei grounds dignity in divine gift prior to autonomy; autonomy-rights grounds dignity in rational self-determination. A natural-law framework might hold both as complementary, but strict theological voluntarism and strict secular autonomy theory are mutually exclusive on the source of dignity.
